notes: Content matrix mirroring table.html. Each cell is a list of clauses; a clause has optional 'label' (bolded prefix in HTML, e.g. 'CA FEHA' or 'Grievance'), 'text' (the clause body), and 'citations' (integer array referencing ids in sources.json/citations). Rows are grouped by row_group (Legal Overview, Content Affected, Conformance Processes). Cells are keyed by column id from sources.json/columns. Column ids ada_title_* and rehab_* also implicitly carry the CA state overlay in cells; state overlays appear as secondary clauses with 'label' set to the state anchor ('CA FEHA', '§11135', 'Unruh', '§7405'). Topical overlays ('Grievance', 'Benchmark', 'Protected', 'Approach') follow the same pattern with a different label. Character conventions: non-breaking hyphens (U+2011) and curly quotes are preserved from the HTML; '<15' and '<5' are stored as literals (HTML escapes them to <).
caption: Federal & California Accessibility Laws: Expert Quick‑Reference (Incorporating CSU ATI Insights & Detailed Legal Context, As of July 18, 2025)

ada_title_i.text: Prohibits discrimination in all aspects of employment (hiring, benefits, workplace systems).

ada_title_i.label: CA FEHA
ada_title_i.text: Covers employers with ≥5 employees; broader “disability” definition (limits major life activity).

ada_title_ii.text: Requires state/local government programs, services, and digital content be equally accessible.
Mirrors Title II for state‑funded activities; CSU ATI leverages this for systemwide accessibility in educational services.

ada_title_iii.text: Ensures private businesses (“public accommodations”) provide equal access to goods/services, including websites/apps.

ada_title_iii.label: Unruh
ada_title_iii.text: ADA violations constitute state‑law violations; broader anti-discrimination in businesses.

rehab_504.text: Prohibits exclusion or denial of benefits in any program/activity receiving federal funds.
Extends non‑discrimination to state‑funded programs; CSU ATI applies this to CSU campuses as state-funded entities.

rehab_508.text: Mandates accessible electronic and information technology for federal agencies.
California state agencies must follow 508 standards; CSU ATI aligns procurement with these for state agencies.

ada_title_i.text: EEOC/DFEH complaints, mediation, lawsuits; FEHA punitive damages allowed.

ada_title_i.label: Grievance
ada_title_i.text: File with EEOC or DFEH within deadlines (180/300 days federal, 3 years CA).

ada_title_ii.text: DOJ investigations, injunctive relief, TA plans.

ada_title_ii.label: Grievance
ada_title_ii.text: File with DOJ or state agency; CSU ATI involves annual reporting; ADA Coordinator required for entities ≥50 employees.

ada_title_iii.text: DOJ enforcement, Unruh private suits; statutory damages per violation ($4k min).

ada_title_iii.label: Grievance
ada_title_iii.text: Civil lawsuits under Unruh; no formal process, direct to court.

rehab_504.text: OCR/HHS complaints, corrective action, funding risk.

rehab_504.label: Grievance
rehab_504.text: File with OCR or agency office; CSU ATI yearly reports track progress; §504 coordinator required for entities ≥15 employees.

rehab_508.text: Procurement holds, vendor CAPs; no private action.

rehab_508.label: Grievance
rehab_508.text: Agency compliance review; CSU ATI uses status levels for auditing; complaints processed like §504.

ada_title_i.text: Employers ≥15 employees; covers employees & applicants with disabilities.

ada_title_i.label: Protected
ada_title_i.text: Mobility, sensory, cognitive, mental health; qualified individuals needing accommodations.

ada_title_ii.text: All state/local government entities; protects individuals accessing public services.

ada_title_ii.label: Protected
ada_title_ii.text: Citizens, students, constituents; CSU ATI emphasizes protection for CSU students, faculty, staff in public university settings.

ada_title_iii.text: Businesses & nonprofits open to the public; protects customers & visitors.

ada_title_iii.label: Protected
ada_title_iii.text: Patrons, online users; includes virtual services.

rehab_504.text: Recipients of federal aid (schools, hospitals, agencies); protects participants.

rehab_504.label: Protected
rehab_504.text: Students, patients, clients; CSU ATI focuses on CSU students and faculty in federally funded programs.

rehab_508.text: Federal agencies and vendors supplying ICT; protects employees & public users.

rehab_508.label: Protected
rehab_508.text: Applicants, citizens; CSU ATI extends to public users of CSU ICT.

ada_title_i.label: Benchmark
ada_title_i.text: WCAG 2.1 AA de facto standard; interactive process for accommodations.

ada_title_ii.text: “Undue burden”/“fundamental alteration” exceptions; requires effective communication.

ada_title_ii.label: Benchmark
ada_title_ii.text: WCAG 2.1 AA (2024 DOJ rule); CSU ATI uses capability maturity model for continuous improvement.

ada_title_iii.text: “Undue burden”/“fundamental alteration” exceptions; auxiliary aids mandated.

ada_title_iii.label: Benchmark
ada_title_iii.text: WCAG 2.1 AA recommended; ADA violations trigger Unruh.

rehab_504.text: Reasonable modifications and auxiliary aids required unless undue hardship.

rehab_504.label: Approach
rehab_504.text: Outcome‑focused; use WCAG as guidance; CSU ATI prioritizes timely accessible formats.

rehab_508.text: “Undue burden” defense; legacy ICT exemptions apply.

rehab_508.label: Benchmark
rehab_508.text: WCAG 2.0 AA per 2017 Refresh; CSU ATI aligns with updated standards; no update to 2.1/2.2 as of 2025.

ada_title_i.text: FEHA SB 1137 (2025): broader “disability” definition; SB 1090 extends claims deadlines.

ada_title_ii.text: DOJ Title II Final Rule (Apr 2024): WCAG 2.1 AA mandate; enforcement trends include increased compliance focus post-deadlines; CSU ATI continues under EO 1111 (2018).

ada_title_iii.text: DOJ Title III regs pending (no final rule as of July 2025); continue WCAG 2.1 AA; SB-84 for cure period stalled.

rehab_504.text: HHS §504 update (2024): WCAG 2.1 AA for health/education portals; deadlines May 2026 (≥15 employees).

rehab_508.text: 508 Refresh (2017) baseline; no refresh to WCAG 2.1/2.2 in 2025; watch for WCAG 2.1/2.2 alignment; CSU ATI promotes ongoing capacity building.

ada_title_i.text: “Undue hardship” defense; “direct threat” to health/safety; must be a “qualified individual” performing essential functions with/without accommodation; religious-organization hiring preference; employers <15 excluded.

ada_title_i.label: CA FEHA
ada_title_i.text: Narrower undue-hardship standard (tied to employer resources); narrow BFOQ defense; religious-association exemption for non-profit religious entities; employers <5 excluded; interactive process required even when hardship is asserted.

ada_title_ii.text: “Fundamental alteration” and “undue financial and administrative burden” defenses (written agency-head finding required); direct threat. 2024 DOJ web-rule carve-outs (as of July 2025): archived web content, pre-existing conventional electronic documents not currently used, password-protected/individualized postsecondary course content, third-party content not posted by or at the direction of the public entity, pre-existing social media posts.
Parallel defenses for CA state‑funded entities; CSU ATI treats carve-outs narrowly and documents each invocation through annual ATI reporting.

ada_title_iii.text: “Undue burden” and “fundamental alteration” defenses; religious entities expressly exempt (including commercial operations); private clubs exempt; “readily achievable” threshold for barrier removal in existing facilities; direct threat.

ada_title_iii.label: Unruh
ada_title_iii.text: No blanket religious-entity exemption for commercial activity—turns on whether entity is a “business establishment”; private-club carve-out construed narrowly; bona-fide defenses require proof.

rehab_504.text: Undue financial/administrative burden; fundamental alteration; direct threat; statute reaches only recipients of federal financial assistance. 2024 HHS §504 web-rule carve-outs (as of July 2025) mirror Title II: archived web content, pre-existing conventional documents, password-protected/individualized content, third-party content, pre-existing social media posts.
Same carve-outs for CA state‑funded programs; CSU ATI documents each exception through yearly ATI reporting.

rehab_508.text: “Undue burden” defense (written documentation by agency official); fundamental alteration; national security systems exempt; legacy ICT exception (pre‑Refresh ICT that is not altered); ICT acquired incidental to a contract; micro-purchase threshold; military tactical/weapons command-and-control systems.
Extends §508 exceptions to CA state agencies; CSU ATI requires written Equivalent Facilitation memos or documented exceptions before completing ICT procurement.

ada_title_i.text: Internal HR/training platforms must support assistive tech (screen readers, keyboard nav), captions—tag PDFs, label forms; equal access via interactive process or alternatives.

ada_title_ii.text: Websites, apps, and documents must meet WCAG 2.1 AA: alt text, color contrast, ARIA, captions; CSU ATI supports through systemwide tools and training.

ada_title_iii.text: Customer‑facing digital services must follow WCAG patterns; dynamic content accessible; provide text alternatives; effective communication via auxiliary aids.

rehab_504.text: Digital content must be accessible or a timely alternate provided: e‑text, captions, Braille, audio descriptions; CSU ATI emphasizes for educational content.

rehab_508.text: ICT must conform to 508/WCAG 2.0 AA: keyboard operability, screen reader support, accessible UIs; CSU ATI provides procurement guidelines.

ada_title_i.text: HR portals, applicant systems, performance dashboards, policy PDFs; online application systems, digital tools.

ada_title_ii.text: Government sites, e‑forms, PDF libraries, emergency alerts, mobile apps; CSU ATI includes university websites and apps.

ada_title_iii.text: E‑commerce sites, booking systems, event registration apps; websites as extensions of services.

rehab_504.text: Course materials, LMS modules, grant portals, telehealth apps; CSU ATI targets Canvas courses, multimedia.

rehab_508.text: Enterprise software, intranet apps, kiosks, digital signage; CSU ATI covers ICT purchases.

ada_title_i.text: Employment websites—job boards, application portals, benefits enrollment, employee self‑service—must support assistive tech and keyboard operation; inaccessible hiring flows trigger failure‑to‑accommodate and disparate‑treatment claims.

ada_title_i.label: CA FEHA
ada_title_i.text: ≥5 employees; web barriers actionable pre‑hire; interactive process extends to digital hiring workflows.

ada_title_ii.text: Public‑entity websites and web apps must meet WCAG 2.1 AA under DOJ's 2024 Title II rule; deadlines April 24, 2026 (populations ≥50,000) and April 26, 2027 (smaller jurisdictions, special districts); narrow exceptions for archived and certain third‑party content.
Parallel obligation for CA state‑funded entities; CSU ATI drives systemwide remediation via automated scans, manual audits, and CMM roadmaps.

ada_title_iii.text: Commercial websites tied to public accommodations (retail, hospitality, banking, ticketing, healthcare) must be accessible; no DOJ Title III web rule as of July 2025—WCAG 2.1 AA remains the de facto litigation benchmark; mobile apps and embedded third‑party components are in scope.

ada_title_iii.label: Unruh
ada_title_iii.text: ADA web violations are per se Civ Code §51 violations; unlocks statutory damages ≥$4,000 per incident in CA state court.

rehab_504.text: Recipient web content—university portals, health‑system patient pages, grant portals, telehealth apps—must meet WCAG 2.1 AA per HHS 2024 §504 update; deadline May 2026 (≥15 employees); no blanket exception for legacy web content.
Mirrors §504 for CA state‑funded programs; CSU ATI folds web remediation into annual ATI reporting.

rehab_508.text: Federal agency public‑facing and intranet websites must conform to Revised 508 (WCAG 2.0 AA per 2017 Refresh); VPATs/ACRs required for COTS web products and SaaS; no update to WCAG 2.1/2.2 as of 2025.
Extends §508 to CA state agencies; CSU ATI aligns web‑platform conformance and vendor ACR review with §508.

ada_title_i.text: Employee training content (manuals, videos) provided in accessible formats as needed upon request (e.g., captioned videos, alternative manuals).

ada_title_i.label: CA FEHA
ada_title_i.text: Includes workplace training accessibility as part of equal benefits.

ada_title_ii.text: Course syllabi, slides, videos, PDFs, LMS content must meet WCAG 2.1 AA by 2026; CSU ATI prioritizes documents, multimedia, Canvas courses for accessibility.
California-funded schools follow same; equal access in education programs.

ada_title_iii.text: Private education providers must supply accessible materials; failure triggers ADA/Unruh claims; accessible examinations and courses required.

rehab_504.text: Provide reasonable modifications—Braille, audio, captions—for instructional content; collaborate with disability services; CSU ATI ensures timely access in federally funded CSU programs.

rehab_508.text: Federally-purchased educational software and e-learning modules must meet 508/WCAG standards; CSU ATI applies to ICT for instructional use.

ada_title_i.text: Employers must procure or adapt assistive technologies to accommodate employees.

ada_title_i.label: CA FEHA
ada_title_i.text: AT procurement for smaller employers; consider accessibility to meet obligations.

ada_title_ii.text: Include accessibility in RFPs, review VPATs, enforce vendor remediation timelines; CSU ATI uses structured procurement process with accessibility reviews.

ada_title_iii.text: Private entities should embed accessibility requirements in purchasing policies to avoid liability; select accessible tech for customer-facing services.

rehab_504.text: Procure accessible products or plan accommodations to ensure program participants are not excluded; CSU ATI ensures compliance in federally funded purchases.

rehab_508.text: Section 508 requires federal agencies to buy 508‑conformant ICT; state agencies follow suit under §7405; CSU ATI reviews ICT for accessibility and security during procurement.
